dpa.title: Data processing agreement
dpa.version: Version {version}. Draft for legal review (docs/21-uae-gcc-strategy.md section 7): the text below states the commitments the platform implements; the reviewed wording replaces it before the first paying tenant.
dpa.roles: You (the customer) are the controller of the personal data your apps process. Renox processes it on your behalf, only to run, store, back up and secure your apps, and only on your documented instructions: your code, your configuration and this agreement.
dpa.where: Tenant databases, files and backups are stored in the hosting region Renox names for the workspace. Moving them to another region needs your written instruction, except where the law requires it.
dpa.security: Each tenant runs in its own isolate with its own database file, per-tenant limits enforced by the platform, outbound requests to private addresses blocked, and secrets encrypted at rest and never written to logs. Operator access to tenant data happens only through a time-boxed, audited break-glass session with a stated reason, and the workspace owner is emailed when one starts and ends.
dpa.subprocessors: The infrastructure, email and payment providers that process data for Renox are listed on the status page; you are told 30 days before a new one is added and may object.
dpa.breaches: Renox tells the workspace owner without undue delay, and within 72 hours, after becoming aware of a personal data breach that affects the workspace, with what is known and the steps taken.
dpa.requests: You can export a database at any time. Erasing a workspace deletes its databases, files, replicas and backups within the retention the dashboard shows, and the erasure record states when it completed.
dpa.acceptance: Accepting this agreement at sign-up records this version and the time on your workspace.

terms.title: Terms of service
terms.version: Version {version}. Draft for legal review: the reviewed wording replaces it before the first paying tenant.
terms.service: Renox hosts TypeScript applications. Your plan sets the quotas; a free workspace that stays over them enters a 7-day grace period and is then suspended until it is back within quota or upgraded. Suspension keeps your data, deployments and dashboard.
terms.use: No phishing, malware, spam, crypto mining, open proxies, or content that is unlawful in the UAE. Reports go to abuse@renox.app; a site found in breach can be taken down at once and reviewed after.
terms.payment: Paid plans are billed monthly in AED with 5 % VAT on a tax invoice. An invoice unpaid 14 days after its date, or a payment dispute, suspends the workspace until it is settled.
terms.data: You own your data and code. The
terms.changes: A new version of these terms is announced 30 days before it applies, by email to the workspace owner.

deploy.rollback_title: Make the previous deployment live again

apps.empty: No apps yet. Create one below, or run

new.we_create_after: and deploy the template to it, then show the commands to work on it locally.

overview.no_logs: No log lines in the last 24 hours.

deployments.explain: Promote makes a validated or earlier deployment live; Rollback makes the previous one live again. Both are a pointer switch after the owning node has prepared the cell, and both are audit-logged.
deployments.advisories_note: A warning from the deployment's SBOM (OSV); nothing is blocked. Update the package and deploy again.

settings.delete_explain: Deleting the tenant removes every app, deployment, secret, domain, log line and meter row, the database on the node and every generation in the replica store, and the exports. It cannot be undone: a point-in-time restore is impossible from then on.
settings.delete_owner: Only the owner can do it, from a signed-in API session (not with a token, so not from this dashboard):

secrets.confirm_delete: Delete {name}? Deployments that declare it lose it from the next deploy or rollback.
secrets.encrypted: Values are encrypted at rest, injected per deployment, and never shown again.

usage.latency_note: Latency is the mean per request of each hour; percentiles (p50, p95) and realtime connections appear when the usage API carries them.
usage.signal_only: In F3 the quota is a signal only: nothing is throttled or suspended when it is exceeded.

errors.intro: Errors that happened in visitors' browsers, grouped by kind, top frame and message.
errors.quota_after: browser events allowed today. Past the cap the gateway drops further events.
errors.regression: Regression: it came back after being resolved.
errors.empty: No browser errors in this view.

database.stale: the node did not answer; this is the last status seen
database.restore_note: A restore creates a new app with this app's active deployment and the database as of the chosen time; this app is not changed.
database.confirm_restore: Restore {app} into a new app? The new app gets its own database and hostname.
database.export_note: A consistent snapshot of the whole file. The link is signed and expires within 15 minutes; your browser downloads it directly. Column masking comes later.

modules.title: Modules
modules.disabled: A module of this app was disabled by Renox.
modules.disabled_note: Running deployments keep running; plan its removal or an upgrade.
modules.none_installed: No registry modules installed. Official modules are listed in renox.toml.

billing.no_tenant: Billing starts with your first app.
billing.owner_only: Billing is managed by the tenant's owner. Ask them to sign in to the dashboard with their own token.
billing.step_up: Payment changes need a code from your authenticator app or a recovery code.
billing.end_of_period: at the end of the period
billing.anomaly: Unusual usage in the last 24 hours is being reviewed.

ops.registry_intro: Operator console. Disabling a version's tree refuses its downloads for every tenant, marks every installation, and emails each tenant owner. Running deployments keep running. Every action needs your operator token (used for this one request, never kept) and a reason of
ops.tenant_intro: Operator console. Every action needs your operator token (it is used for this one request and never kept) and a reason of
ops.characters_audit: characters, which goes into the audit row with your account.
ops.no_replication: No node has reported this tenant's replication yet.
ops.no_actions: No operator action on this tenant yet.
ops.break_glass_note: For 60 minutes, read only (apps, logs, secret names). This dashboard session signs in as the impersonation, every request is audited as yours with the reason, and the tenant's owner is emailed at the start and the end. It needs a token created with
ops.confirm_impersonate: Read {tenant}'s data for 60 minutes? Its owner is emailed now.
ops.confirm_tier: Change the tier of {tenant}? Its route entries are republished with the new process tier.
ops.confirm_node: Move {tenant}? Its file is restored on the node first, then its routes change and the old node drains it.
ops.microvm_note: The tenant answers 503 while the node's hook runs. In F6 the hook is a stub that exits 75, and the tenant stays where it is.
ops.confirm_microvm: Move {tenant} to a microVM? Its requests answer 503 while the hook runs.
